hints: Calculate all four side lengths: $PQ = QR = RS = SP = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5$.
Examine the diagonals: $P(-2, 1)$ to $R(6, 1)$ is horizontal, and $Q(2, 4)$ to $S(2, -2)$ is vertical.
Since all four sides are equal and horizontal/vertical lines are perpendicular, $PQRS$ is a rhombus.
walkthrough:
Four equal sides prove a rhombus; perpendicular diagonals give its area.
Calculate the lengths of all four sides:
$$PQ = \sqrt{(2 - (-2))^2 + (4 - 1)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$
$$QR = \sqrt{(6 - 2)^2 + (1 - 4)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$
$$RS = \sqrt{(2 - 6)^2 + (-2 - 1)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$
$$SP = \sqrt{(-2 - 2)^2 + (1 - (-2))^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5$$
All four sides are equal in length ($5$ units).

Verify that the diagonals are perpendicular:
$$PR \text{ lies on the horizontal line } y = 1 \implies m_{PR} = 0$$
$$QS \text{ lies on the vertical line } x = 2 \implies m_{QS} \text{ is undefined}$$
Horizontal and vertical lines are perpendicular ($PR \perp QS$). Therefore, $PQRS$ is a rhombus.

hints: Apply the rhombus area formula: $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times d_1 \times d_2$.
walkthrough:
Four equal sides prove a rhombus; perpendicular diagonals give its area.
Calculate the lengths of the diagonals $PR$ and $QS$:
$$PR = |6 - (-2)| = 8$$
$$QS = |4 - (-2)| = 6$$

Calculate the area of the rhombus:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PR \times QS = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 6 = 24$$
